blocks.text: Polyatomic ions are ions composed of more than one type of atom. Their formal charge is the net charge on them, calculated from the number of electrons in their valence shells after the bonds have formed. With the exception of the ammonium ion NH4+, these ions mostly carry a negative charge, for example carbonate CO3 2-, sulfate SO4 2- and nitrate NO3 -. In some polyatomic ions the central atom violates the octet rule by expanding its electron density into higher orbitals; these are said to have expanded octets. Prominent examples are SO4 2-, ClO4 - and PO4 3-.

blocks.alt: Lewis structure of the sulfate ion in square brackets with charge 2- at the top right. Sulfur is in the centre with double bonds to the oxygen atoms above and below it and single bonds to the oxygen atoms on the left and right. Each double-bonded oxygen has two lone pairs and each single-bonded oxygen has three lone pairs. The words 'sulfate ion' are written inside the brackets.
blocks.caption: Lewis structure of the sulfate ion (original drawing after the structure printed beside the text in the textbook).

blocks.text: From the Lewis structure of SO4 2-, the number of electrons around the central sulfur atom is 2 x (double bond electrons) + 2 x (single bond electrons) = 2(4) + 2(2) = 12. So sulfur has 12 electrons in its valence shell and exceeds the octet by four. The expansion is caused by the involvement of the d orbital in bonding, which can accommodate the extra electrons. The configuration of a native S(0) atom shows two unpaired electrons in the 3p orbitals; the presence of the 3d orbital allows this to extend to four unpaired electrons by the transfer of one electron from the 3p pair. This explains not only the variable oxidation states of sulfur but also its ability to accept extra electrons in its d orbital.

blocks.alt: Two rows of orbital boxes for sulfur, each with one 3s box, three 3p boxes and five 3d boxes. Top row: 3s has a pair of opposite arrows, 3p has one pair and two single up arrows, 3d is empty. Bottom row: 3s has one up arrow, each 3p box has one up arrow, and the first two 3d boxes have one up arrow each.
blocks.caption: Electron boxes of sulfur: 3s, 3p and 3d orbitals before and after promotion of electrons (original drawing after the box diagrams printed in the textbook).

blocks.alt: Lewis structure of the tri-iodide ion: three iodine atoms in a line, I-I-I, joined by two single bonds. Each iodine atom carries three lone pairs. The structure is in square brackets with a minus charge at the top right.
blocks.caption: Lewis structure of the tri-iodide ion, [I3]- (original drawing after the structure printed in the textbook).

blocks.text: In the same way, the valence electrons around the central iodine atom of the tri-iodide ion I3- are 2 x (single bond electrons) + 2 x (lone pairs) = 2(2) + 2(3) = 10. The central iodine has 10 electrons in its valence shell, and the octet expands by two.
